0.0.n: Connects this purchase to what the speaker mentioned before.

0.2.n: Describes ゲーム directly, without needing a linking word.

0.3.n: This borrowed word can mean one game or several; the number here makes it plural.

0.4.n: Marks ゲーム as what the speaker bought.

0.5.n: Combines with つ to make 三つ, the general counting expression for three things.

0.6.n: A general counter for things; here it counts games.

0.7.n: The polite past form of 買う, showing that the purchase is complete.

1.0.n: The name of the game franchise.

1.1.n: Links the franchise name ポケモン to the specific title バイオレット.

1.2.n: The name of this Pokémon game version, not a description of its color.

1.3.n: Links this game title to the next item in the list.

2.0.n: The name of a video game series.

2.1.n: Part of the title Splatoon 3, identifying the installment rather than counting games.

2.2.n: Connects Splatoon 3 to the final game title.

3.0.n: A name forming the first part of the game title Super Mario Odyssey.

3.2.n: The final part of the game title Super Mario Odyssey.

3.3.n: Politely completes the identification of the three games, covering the whole list.

4.0.n: The franchise name introduces what the speaker is talking about.

4.1.n: Marks ポケモン as the topic, while 私 identifies the person who played.

4.2.n: The speaker names herself as the player; a following particle is omitted in this casual speech.

4.4.n: Combines with の時 to describe the period when the speaker was a child.

4.5.n: Connects 子供 to 時, forming an expression meaning when someone was a child.

4.6.n: In 子供の時, it refers to the speaker’s childhood.

4.7.n: Marks childhood as the starting point of the speaker’s experience.

4.8.n: Emphasizes continuing involvement over the period since childhood, not necessarily nonstop playing.

4.9.n: Refers to Pokémon video games as something the speaker played.

4.10.n: Adds games to other Pokémon-related interests or activities, which are not specified in this line.

4.11.n: Short for やっていた, from やる; here it describes an ongoing past habit of playing.

4.12.n: Short for の in んです, presenting the speaker’s history as background for the next point.

4.13.n: Adds politeness to the explanation in やってたんです.

4.14.n: Leaves the thought open and leads into a contrast with recent Pokémon games.

5.0.n: With の, it describes the newer Pokémon games rather than when the change happened.

5.1.n: Connects 最近 to ポケモン to specify recent entries in the franchise.

5.2.n: The franchise name stands for its games here.

5.3.n: Marks recent Pokémon games as the topic of the observation.

5.4.n: The polite past form of 変わる, describing a change the speaker has noticed.

5.5.n: Invites agreement with the speaker’s observation, giving it a conversational tone.

6.0.n: The franchise name here refers to the creatures encountered in the game.

6.1.n: Marks ポケモン as what was different.

6.2.n: Although often paired with negatives, 全然 also emphasizes difference with 違う.

6.3.n: The polite past form of 違う, comparing the Pokémon with those the speaker knew before.

0.lit: And then, new games, three items, I bought.
0.tip: Japanese can place the quantity after the object: ゲームを3つ買いました.

1.tip: と links game titles in a list that continues across subtitle lines.

2.tip: Here 3 belongs to the game’s name; it does not count how many games were bought.

3.tip: The final です completes the whole list, not just the last title.

4.lit: As for Pokémon, I, since childhood, all along, games also was playing, you see, but…
4.tip: やってた is conversational shorthand for やっていた, describing a past ongoing activity or habit.

5.lit: As for recent Pokémon, they changed, haven’t they?
5.tip: 最近のポケモン means recent Pokémon games, while final ね invites the listener to agree.

6.tip: 全然違う is a common combination meaning completely different, even though there is no negative ending.
